Normal-variant guard is the controlling constraint: asymptomatic minor septal deviation is present in the majority of the population (Alghamdi 2022), so any individual claim must document clinically significant obstruction (symptoms plus examination or CT severity) rather than the anatomic variant alone.
governanceNotes: Both edges authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY with NOT_ESTABLISHED consensus and hypothesizedOnly mechanisms despite standard mechanical biology (ostiomeatal obstruction; nasal-airway resistance): the quantified anchors are a referred CT population (OR 2.74) and a small PSG cohort (n=60); deviation is one of many CRS comorbidities in the global meta-analysis; and craniofacial development is a documented shared upstream driver of both deviation and OSA anatomy (Hutz 2024), so direction cannot be fixed at the population level.

Combined-pathology guard: the OSA cohort found combined nasal pathologies carried proportionately more OSA than isolated septal deviation, so isolated-anatomy attribution requires excluding concurrent polyps, adenoid hypertrophy, turbinate hypertrophy, and allergic rhinitis.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cross-sectional CT-referral cohort (n=676) found patients with deviated nasal septum approximately three times more likely to have sinusitis (OR 2.74, CI 1.86-4.04) (Alsaggaf 2022); the 28-study global meta-analysis lists septal deviation among comorbid conditions with greater chronic-rhinosinusitis prevalence (Min 2025); the prevention review names septal deviation among sinonasal risk factors for recurrent sinusitis (Duse 2007).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the ostiomeatal-obstruction pathway is standard anatomy-to-infection biology, but the quantified anchor is a CT-referral population with ascertainment bias (both CT referral and sinus findings concentrate in symptomatic patients); deviation is one of several comorbidities in the meta-analysis rather than an isolated driver; and recurrent-sinusitis etiology is multifactorial (infection, allergy, smoke, immune status) in the same sources.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized drainage-obstruction pathway: septal deviation narrows or occludes the nasal cavity on the convex side, displacing turbinate structures and compromising mucociliary clearance at the ostiomeatal complex; retained mucus and impaired ventilation create a low-oxygen environment favoring bacterial proliferation; recurrent acute episodes or chronic inflammation produce sinusitis with laterality often tracking the deviation. Recurrence persists until the anatomic factor is corrected or the mucosal disease is controlled.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Referred-population ascertainment (CT cohorts are enriched for both findings); multifactorial sinusitis etiology (viral, allergic, smoke, immune); laterality correspondence is absent in a meaningful minority; and no general-population incidence cohort - association strength is the supportable ceiling.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: CT-documented clinically significant deviation with ostiomeatal narrowing and corresponding sinus disease; recurrent or chronic course; exclusion of allergic, tobacco, dental, and immune drivers

evidenceGaps: CT documentation of clinically significant deviation (not the normal-variant spectrum) with ostiomeatal narrowing and corresponding sinus involvement
recurrence or chronicity documentation (multiple treated episodes or CRS criteria) rather than a single episode
exclusion of allergic rhinitis, tobacco exposure, dental-source infection, and immune deficiency as primary drivers
laterality or anatomical correspondence between the deviation and the sinusitis where claimed
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: quantified support comes from a referred CT population with multifactorial competing etiologies; no causal claim is forced.

sourceReferences.note: Prevention review: sinonasal abnormalities including septal deviation are risk factors for recurrent sinusitis alongside infection, adenoid bacterial load, and smoke exposure; prevention requires treating the associated conditions.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The polysomnography-confirmed cohort (n=60) found isolated septal deviation significantly associated with the occurrence and severity of obstructive sleep apnea, with combined nasal pathologies carrying proportionately more OSA (Shankameswaran 2024); the narrative review lists OSA among the clinical presentations of clinically significant deviation (Alghamdi 2022); the prospective sleep-surgery cohort documents craniofacial development as a shared upstream driver linking maxillary deficiency to both deviation and OSA anatomy (Hutz 2024).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: nasal-obstruction contribution to OSA is mechanistically plausible (increased upper-airway resistance, mouth breathing, suction-collapse) but nasal obstruction is a minor contributor in most OSA phenotypes; the PSG cohort is small (n=60); the shared craniofacial substrate (Hutz 2024) means deviation and OSA can co-develop without one causing the other; and septoplasty trials show incomplete OSA response, confirming deviation is not a sufficient cause.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized nasal-airway-resistance pathway: clinically significant septal deviation increases nasal resistance, promotes mouth breathing during sleep, and may enhance pharyngeal suction collapse through the Starling-resistor effect; the resulting repetitive apneas and hypopneas produce the OSA phenotype. The pathway is phenotype-dependent - it plausibly contributes most in patients whose obstruction is primarily nasal - and obesity-related pharyngeal narrowing operates independently in the same patients.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Small PSG cohort; shared craniofacial substrate confound; deviation insufficient as a sole cause (incomplete post-septoplasty OSA resolution in the literature); obesity/BMI as a dominant independent driver - all keep the claim at association strength.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: PSG-confirmed OSA with CT-documented clinically significant deviation; NOSE-score nasal-obstruction support; exclusion of polyps, adenoid hypertrophy, and turbinate hypertrophy; BMI documentation to weight the obesity pathway
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Craniofacial deficiency as a shared driver (maxillary deficiency)

evidenceGaps: polysomnographic confirmation of OSA (AHI with severity grading) with CT-documented clinically significant deviation
nasal-obstruction documentation (NOSE score or equivalent) supporting the nasal pathway in that individual
exclusion of combined pathologies (polyps, adenoid hypertrophy, turbinate hypertrophy) and of obesity-dominant phenotype
documentation of BMI and neck circumference to weight the competing drivers
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: PSG-anchored occurrence/severity association with a documented shared-substrate confound and a minor-contributor mechanism; no causal claim is forced.

sourceReferences.citation: Shankameswaran B, Viveknarayan G, Gowrishankar M, Suresh V. Prevalence of Obstructive Sleep Apnoea in patients with primary nasal and nasopharyngeal pathologies. Indian J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2024;76(5):3914-3921. PMID 39376455.
sourceReferences.note: Polysomnography-confirmed cohort (n=60): isolated septal deviation, nasal polyps, and adenoid hypertrophy each showed statistically significant association with the occurrence and severity of obstructive sleep apnea; combined pathologies affected OSA proportionately more than isolated ones.

sourceReferences.citation: Alghamdi FS, Albogami D, Alsurayhi AS, et al. Nasal Septal Deviation: A Comprehensive Narrative Review. Cureus. 2022;14(11):e31317. PMID 36514566.
sourceReferences.note: Narrative review: asymptomatic minor deviation is a normal developmental variant in the majority of the population; clinically significant deviation can obstruct nasal airflow and is associated with rhinosinusitis and obstructive sleep apnea among its presentations - the minor-variant guard for any deviated-septum claim.

sourceReferences.citation: Hutz MJ, Thuler E, Cheong C, et al. The Association Between Transverse Maxillary Deficiency and Septal Deviation in Adults with Obstructive Sleep Apnea. Laryngoscope. 2024;134(5):2464-2470. PMID 37905744.
sourceReferences.note: Prospective CT cohort of sleep-surgery patients (n=93): transverse maxillary deficiency is moderately associated with greater septal deviation, supporting craniofacial development as a shared upstream driver of both the deviation and the sleep-apnea anatomy - the shared-substrate (reverse/confound) guard.
